title: 76% of Australians are struggling to tell apart real and AI content – new report
headline: Survey finds 76% of Australians struggle to distinguish AI-generated from human content
summary: A survey of 2,000 Australian adults reveals that 76% have recently encountered content they mistakenly believed was real before discovering it was AI-generated. Despite high awareness of AI tools, trust in major platforms remains low, and most users rely on intuition rather than formal verification methods to assess content authenticity. The findings highlight a significant gap in public AI literacy and a strong demand for clearer labelling and safety guardrails.
why_it_matters: The findings underscore an urgent need for organisations to implement transparent AI labelling and robust safety frameworks to address low public trust and the widespread inability of users to identify synthetic content.

quotes.text: Our new representative survey of 2,000 Australian adults conducted in August and September 2026 found 76% of Australians had recently encountered content they initially believed was real, only to later discover it had been generated by AI.

First, digital platforms need clearer and more consistent labelling of AI-generated content. If people are expected to make informed decisions about what they’re seeing, they need transparent information about where that content comes from.

classification.significance_reason: Provides empirical evidence of public sentiment and literacy gaps in Australia, informing the context for future AI governance and labelling requirements.
